families.title: Engine, render passes, batches, compute stages
families.reason: A program names adapters and their config, never the engine's methods. The host makes the passes and the camera; instances use the 14-float layout; every batch is opaque, depth on, both faces drawn.
families.summary: The NullGraph engine owns the WebGPU device and runs an explicit, ordered sequence of compute stages and render passes; there is no scene graph, no parenting and no automatic light. A batch is one pipeline drawing many instances from a storage buffer; a compute stage dispatches one WGSL kernel. Every other family plugs into this sequence.
notes: Lifecycle: init and check its success; create passes, batches and compute stages; render(sequence) each frame; destroy when done.
Bind groups: group 0 is the camera and the batch's instance storage, group 1 the material; lit materials put lights and environment at group 2 and shadows take the last: all four are spent.
Order: producers before consumers: light binning, culling and shadow passes before the draws that use them, post after its inputs.

families.title: Primitives, vertex layouts, packed meshes
families.reason: ng.geometry.primitive: the thirteen primitives and the host's ground, from one size (fixed proportions) and segments. The plane stands upright (XY, facing +Z). No custom geometry, megabuffers or meshlets.
families.summary: Pure CPU math: thirteen primitives (cube, sphere, plane, cylinder, cone, capsule, torus, ring, pyramid, octahedron, tetrahedron, icosahedron, dodecahedron) and custom geometry as typed arrays with a vertex layout, uploaded once and bound to a batch with setBatchGeometry. Megabuffers and meshlets feed the visibility system.
notes: Primitives take explicit sizes and segment counts; geometry.upload(engine) before binding it.
A batch's vertexLayouts must match its geometry: geometry.layout.getWebGPUDescriptor().

families.title: GLB parsing, skeletons, baked animation
families.reason: Needs GLB asset files; Wexy has no asset allowlist, so a program cannot name one.
families.summary: GLBParser reads binary glTF into vertex layouts, indices, textures, skeletons and animation channels; Animator and SkeletonManager drive skinned meshes; the bake functions turn clips into poses sampled on the GPU. Material colour factors and vertex colours are not kept.

families.title: Stock materials and their shader builders
families.reason: ng.material.stock: kind and baseColor only, no maps (matcap is refused). Basic, lambert, toon and emissive multiply baseColor by the instance colour; pbr ignores it and draws as a rough metal.
families.summary: Each material is a shader builder (build*Shader: WGSL for the batch's pipeline) plus a class that owns its uniforms and textures and binds them at group 1 with applyToBatch: Basic (unlit), Lambert, Toon, Matcap, Emissive and StandardPBR. buildMaterialFragment and the WGSL chunks let a custom shader reuse the same lighting.
notes: Stock vertex shaders read 14 floats an instance: [0] unused, [1..3] position, [4..7] rotation quaternion (w = 1 for none), [8..10] scale, [11..13] color.
Lit builders (Lambert, Toon, PBR) take lighting = lightSystem.getShaderLayout(); without it each falls back to one fixed key light. Basic, Emissive and Matcap use no light.
PBR wants albedo, normal and packed maps: the engine's fallback textures serve when there are none.

families.title: GPU timestamp queries
families.reason: Wexy's host measures GPU time itself; a program never asks for it.
families.summary: GPUProfiler wraps WebGPU timestamp queries to report how long the GPU spent on work, through a callback; it needs the optional timestamp-query feature and does nothing without it.

families.title: Telemetry widgets and debug drawings
families.reason: Developer overlays and debug drawings; never part of a world.
families.summary: Widgets that draw FPS and CPU and GPU timing into the frame, and debug drawings (ground grids, agent arrows, grid occupancy) for development.

families.title: Camera controllers
families.reason: Wexy's host owns the camera: it frames the world when shown, and the creator orbits it and sets its keyframes. A program cannot move it: a world must read well from any side.
families.summary: Orbital, fly, follow and path camera states (pure math producing the eye and target for Camera.updateView), with optional DOM event proxies, decoupled so they can run in a worker.

families.title: Data-oriented lights
families.reason: ng.light.rig: ambient, at most one directional and four point lights, set once at init (they never move); standard technique. The ambient arrives from straight above: downward faces get none. Only lambert, toon and pbr are lit.
families.summary: Lights are 16-float slices in one Float32Array written through cursor proxies (directional, point, spot, ambient, hemisphere, rect area, torch). LightSystem supplies the matching WGSL (getShaderLayout) for lit materials and, for the tiled and clustered techniques, a compute stage that bins the lights before the draws.
notes: Techniques: none; standard (every fragment loops every light: small counts); tiled-forward and clustered-forward (a binning compute stage each frame). One shader contract for all.
Lighting lives at group 2, shared with the environment.

families.title: Post-processing chain
families.reason: ng.post.chain: the sixteen built-in effects, one intensity each (0 to 4), run in the program's order; no CustomEffect. Without a chain the background is a fixed dark grey.
families.summary: PostChain runs screen-space effects after the scene pass: engine.render([scenePass, ...post.getPassSequence()]). Sixteen built-in effects (AutoExposure, Bloom, Bokeh, CelShade, ChromaticAberration, ColorGrade, FXAA, FilmGrain, GodRays, Halation, Kuwahara, LensFlare, Outline, SSAO, Tonemap, Vignette) and CustomEffect, a WGSL fn effect(uv: vec2f) -> vec4f over the chain's input, and the depth when asked.
notes: Effects own no GPU objects: the chain allocates and aliases the targets and keeps every parameter in one uniform buffer.
setChain (or compile) before getPassSequence, upload or resize; the scene pass renders into the chain's attachments.

families.title: GPU-driven culling and LOD
families.summary: VisibilitySystem culls on the GPU (frustum, meshlet normal cones, Hi-Z occlusion) and draws indirectly, so draw calls scale with meshes and materials, not instances. Instances are 24-float records in an InstanceBuffer over a megabuffer; its compute stages run before the pass that draws.
notes: 24-float records, not the stock materials' 14: a material needs the visibility bridge (the shader reference).
Hi-Z needs a samplable depth and the previous frame's depth.

families.title: Shadow maps and the shadow atlas
families.summary: Cascaded shadow maps for a sun, then one atlas for every light type with tiles sized by importance; casters are culled on the GPU and drawn depth-only, and receivers sample through decorators that drop into the existing materials.
notes: Shadow passes run before the draws that sample them; shadows take the last bind group.

families.title: Sky, image-based lighting, probes, atmosphere, fog
families.summary: Indirect light and skies: EnvironmentSystem (a prefiltered cube, SH-L2, a BRDF table) injects getIndirectDiffuse and getIndirectSpecular into lit materials as LightSystem injects direct light. Sky models (gradient, equirect, physical atmosphere, night sky, star field, time of day), probe volumes and reflection probes, aerial perspective and height fog.
notes: Bakes and the shadow atlas are submitted before probe prewarm; environment passes run before the draws that sample them.
Without it, PBR's indirect term is a constant ambient.

families.title: What is under a pixel
families.summary: Picker answers which source, instance, depth and world position lie under a pixel, for plain batches and visibility instances, with a small render of its own off the frame path and a readback.

families.title: World-anchored labels
families.summary: TextSystem draws hundreds of thousands of screen-space labels anchored to world points in one GPU-culled draw, from SDF glyph atlases (FontAtlas, layoutText); labels can follow positions only the GPU knows.

families.title: GPU agents and their brains
families.summary: AgentSystem runs many agents on the GPU on a fixed step: sense, think (rule brains or MlpBrain networks), act, with neighbour grids and per-species brains; the app's own stages join the step. Training happens outside the package.

families.title: Networks from files
families.reason: Needs a trained network file, and for OrtBrain the optional ONNX Runtime, which the studio does not ship.
families.summary: mlpFromOnnx reads a small dense network from .onnx bytes for MlpBrain; OrtRuntime, OrtModel and OrtBrain run larger models through ONNX Runtime Web's WebGPU provider.

families.title: Disc contacts
families.summary: DiscContacts separates overlapping discs on the XZ plane in a caller-owned GPU record buffer, as stages after movement on each fixed step; it neither integrates motion nor renders bodies.

families.title: Offline film rendering
families.reason: Wexy's host films every world through the studio's export; a program never calls it.
families.summary: Deterministic offline rendering in the browser: a managed runner, readback, video encoding (with the optional mediabunny), storage to OPFS or a picked file, PNG sequences and snapshots.
